There's only 2 reference voltages, and they're trivially detectable (we only use 3 models of BMC)  Why would we add values to every sensor on every platform rather than just make the ADC base detected in code?

> There's only 2 reference voltages, and they're trivially detectable (we only use 3 models of BMC) 

When we use the iio-hwmon dirver to detect the ADC sensors, the linux kernel of iio-hwmon does not include the reference voltage values. If we add one more property for ADC to present reference voltage, it is not clear to map reference voltage to Max/MinValue of sensors.

> Why would we add values to every sensor on every platform rather than just make the ADC base detected in code?

Some sensors like FAN/PSU also support configuration Max/MinValue. About others applications, I don't know the current status of them, that why I only add Max/MinValue configuration for ADC and Hwmon-temp in this commit.

> > There's only 2 reference voltages, and they're trivially detectable (we only use 3 models of BMC) 
> 
> When we use the iio-hwmon dirver to detect the ADC sensors, the linux kernel of iio-hwmon does not include the reference voltage values. If we add one more property for ADC to present reference voltage, it is not clear to map reference voltage to Max/MinValue of sensors.

No, but it makes it clear what the property is used for.  "min/max" value would have to be computed by hand otherwise.

> 
> > Why would we add values to every sensor on every platform rather than just make the ADC base detected in code?
> 
> Some sensors like FAN/PSU also support configuration Max/MinValue. About others applications, I don't know the current status of them, that why I only add Max/MinValue configuration for ADC and Hwmon-temp in this commit.

Right, because those sensors don't support scaling, so they're reading a known value.

> No, but it makes it clear what the property is used for.  "min/max" value would have to be computed by hand otherwise.

Yes, users have to calculate the Max/MinValue. But I think this is more meaningful for users to understand the purpose of thos properties. Beside that, I want to unify the method to configure Max/MinValue properties between sensors type.

Looking over the code here again, I think I see what Ed's getting at -- 

If we only have a handful of supported ACDSensors

As I understand it, this PR would add the option for defining min/max values (that would need some calculations I don't understand applied) at the entity-manager config level for ADCsensor stanzas.

-- but leaving Min/Max blank would still continue on with today's behavior as the default.

This seems like an improvement to me, even if the ideal option would have the ADCSensor daemon recognize "oh hey, it's this type of ADC" and set the correct min/max automatically -- I'm not too sure how that would look, since I don't see compatible string lookups happening in there like I'm used to seeing in FanSensor cod I've been digging in...

Maybe it'd be as simple as adding a compatible string lookup, and matching against a list of known ADC compatible strings and setting a max value there?

A little more complicated, but would save folks the trouble of having to calculate/pass around numbers for the same pieces of HW and plug them into every EntityManager stanza making use of that HW.

I wonder if starting that as a separate PR for discussion could be worthwhile re: letting this part move forward without that element?

@Christopher.Sides+GitHub@gmail.com, the adcsensor is setting the Max/min values properties based on the Vref value of hardware (the default vaule is 1.8V as https://github.com/openbmc/dbus-sensors/blob/master/src/adc/ADCSensor.cpp#L50). The MaxValue is `Vref/scaleFactor` as https://github.com/openbmc/dbus-sensors/blob/master/src/adc/ADCSensor.cpp#L62, MinValue is 0. Ed suggested to add Vref property in the EM.


> Looking over the code here again, I think I see what Ed's getting at --
>
> If we only have a handful of supported ACDSensors

Adding Max/Min values in the EM for ADC sensors makes it easier for users to understand the purpose of those properties, even though they have to calculate them from the Vref value. Besides that, it makes consistency between applications in the dbus-sensors.

I'm still really not sure why we don't have a (compile time or runtime) check that just sets all BMC ADC values to a 1.8 or 3.3v source.  We can't have a mix, so putting it in the per-platform configuration when a given image can only have one or the other doesn't make sense and duplicates a lot of code.

What I suspect is that we're trying to adjust the min/max values to provide better ranging somewhere else and let redfish represent different min/max values.

> AAdding Max/Min values in the EM for ADC sensors makes it easier for users to understand the purpose of those properties, even though they have to calculate them from the Vref value

one very important thing that EM configs do is they do not push implementation details into the config.  Thresholds in the config file should be in volts, any conversion for ranging should be done in the sensor daemon itself.
I am not sure that all ADC sensors in a platform have same Vref value, I think it depend on the hardware design.
Done
Can we do something to make parsing of these properties common, and not spread around the code-base?

> Can we do something to make parsing of these properties common, and not spread around the code-base?

The FAN sensors are getting Max/MinValue from the MaxReading/MinReading properties in the EM configuration, the PSU sensors are getting the Max/MinValue base on the <label>_Max/Min properties. Therefore, we can not have a common solution for this issue.
Do you have any comments for this commit?

As I understand the code, this fix replaces hardcoded 'min' and 'max' values (voltage for ADCSensor, temp for HwmonTempSensor) with a version of the values that get read in from Entity-Manager configs (if the values are defined for a given record the JSON config).

As I understand it, before this fix, 'MinValue' and 'MaxValue' have been valid Entity-Manager record properties, but it seems like no daemons were actually reading in the values outside of the external sensors daemon.

The changes seem to make sense to me.
Your understading is correct. I just want to add one more point, some sensors like External/AirTemp are using `Max/MinValue` properties in the Entity-Manager to set the range of sensor's value
Do you have any comments for this commit?
lgtm

I believe fixing the EM schemas should come first, then think about adding new properties after that's been done.

Other than that i have no relevant opinion on this change 😊

Ed had some questions asked earlier, but seems like that all got replied to...
As written, this looks like it breaks every ADC config that doesn't have an explicit min/max?
I set the default maximum value of adc sensor is 1.8v/ScaleFactor and minimun is 0. If the EM configuration does not have Max/Min value, the default values shall be used.
ScaleFactor looks like it's now completely ignored.  We cannot assume that all configs will have a min/max set, so you'll need to implement fallback behavior.

> ScaleFactor looks like it's now completely ignored

The `ScaleFactor` is need to convert raw date in the hardware to the double value, refer to https://github.com/openbmc/dbus-sensors/blob/master/src/adc/ADCSensor.cpp#L221 for more information.

> We cannot assume that all configs will have a min/max set, so you'll need to implement fallback behavior.

I set the default maximum value of adc sensor is `1.8v/ScaleFactor` and minimun is 0. If the EM configuration does not have Max/Min value, the default values shall be used.
I created struct SensorRange in the `sensor.hpp` file as your suggestion.
Not all BMCs are 1.8 VREF
To avoid impacting to other platforms, if they do not have Max/Min properties in the EM then the maximum value shall be `1.8V/scalefactor` as current implementation.
Phrasing.  I'm not sure what this is trying to say.  Maybe "almost all sensors" ?

please refactor so that this function doesn't get any larger with your change.

Other things in this file use VariantToFloatVisitor. SHoudl we be consistent?
Moved to independent getSensorRange function to get sensor range.
Please make sure you check for divide by 0 and NAN before using these in math.  I realize the code before was unsafe as well, but we should fix that.
specificaly, check for "isfinite(scaleFactor) && scaleFactor != 0.0"
I updated line 256 to check `scaleFactor`.

> This confuses me.  We now effectively do
> 
> range.minimum = thisSensorParameters.minValue

This step sets the default value of sensor's range.

> getSensorRange();

The `getSensorRange` function updates the sensor's range if the base configuration includes `MaxValue/MinValue` properties, else the range will be the default values.

> thisSensorParameters.minValue = range.minimum;

Update the sensor parameters based on the calculated range.

> 
> It's not clear to me why we do that.
> 
> Probably you just want to have getSensorRange return SensorRange directly?

If the base configuration does not include `MaxVaue/MinValue`, we can not return SensorRange directly. I also update the name of `getSensorRange` to `updateSensorRange`.
